part1_item1.notes:
[chunk 1/2] Key findings from MSFT 10-Q (FY26 Q2, period ending Dec 31 2025):

1. OPENAI CIRCULARITY (Severity 4): MSFT holds ~27% of OpenAI (equity method, HLBV), has committed $13B total ($11.7B funded), sells Azure compute to OpenAI, AND books P&L from OpenAI equity gains. Q2 FY26 net income was inflated by ~$10B dilution gain from OpenAI Recapitalization — a non-cash item representing ~26% of quarterly net income of $38.5B.

2. OpenAI is a VIE NOT consolidated (Severity 3): Despite 27% ownership and $13B commitment, MSFT determined it is not primary beneficiary. OpenAI debt/liabilities are entirely off MSFT balance sheet.

3. CAPEX ROI GAP (Severity 4): H1 FY26 capex $49.3B vs $30.7B H1 FY25 (+60% YoY). PP&E grew $67B gross in 6 months. AP for PP&E jumped from $6.9B to $23.1B — suggesting accelerating unbooked commitments. Depreciation at $15B/half-year implies multi-year payback horizon with no matched contracted revenue disclosed.

4. SERVER COMPONENT RECEIVABLES (Severity 2): $15.1B "other receivables related to activities to facilitate purchase of server components" — nearly doubled from $8.2B in 6 months. This is quasi-supply-chain financing that doesn't appear in capex or debt.

5. HLBV COST OPACITY (Severity 3): Non-standard equity method accounting for OpenAI makes income recognition opaque and non-comparable. $10B Q2 gain is from dilution event, not operating performance.

No named SPV/JV structures or third-party off-balance-sheet entities (e.g., Blue Owl, Brookfield) disclosed in this section. No individual investee names beyond OpenAI appear in the equity investments footnote in this filing section.
[chunk 2/2] KEY FINDINGS FROM MSFT 10-Q (Dec 31 2025):

1. HIDDEN LEVERAGE – UNCOMMENCED LEASES ($155.1B): The single most material signal. MSFT discloses $155.1B of datacenter leases not yet commenced (off-balance-sheet obligation), on top of $60.2B already on-balance finance lease liabilities and $22.9B operating lease liabilities. The uncommenced leases represent a future obligation roughly 3.5x the current on-balance finance lease stack, and nearly equal to MSFT's entire annual revenue. These will begin hitting the balance sheet FY2026–FY2031.

2. OPENAI RECAPITALIZATION: Referenced only in the tax note — MSFT recognized a "dilution gain from the OpenAI Recapitalization" which drove deferred tax expense, pushing effective tax rate from 18% to 20%. This signals a structural change in MSFT's equity stake in OpenAI (likely conversion to capped-profit PBC structure), but no dollar amount or new equity % is disclosed in this section.

3. IRS NOPAs ($28.9B): IRS seeking $28.9B in additional taxes plus penalties and interest for tax years 2004–2013 (intercompany transfer pricing). MSFT believes its reserves are adequate but does not expect resolution in next 12 months. Severity 3 — material but not novel.

4. CAPEX ROI GAP: Finance lease ROU assets grew $19.3B gross in 6 months (to $73.2B). Finance lease liabilities grew $14B to $60.2B. Combined with $155.1B uncommenced, and $631B RPO backlog at 2.5yr weighted avg, the infrastructure buildout is racing ahead of contracted revenue realization.

5. No individual customer exceeded 10% of revenue — customer concentration risk is confirmed absent per explicit disclosure.

part2_item1a.notes:
[chunk 1/2] MSFT 10-Q (2026-01-28) Item 1A extraction. Key SIFI-material findings:

1. CIRCULARITY (Severity 4): Microsoft is simultaneously investor in, compute infrastructure provider to, and AI model consumer from OpenAI. The October 2025 "significant update" to the partnership was explicitly cited, deepening this circular dependency without quantified terms in this section.

2. CAPEX ROI GAP (Severity 3): Management explicitly warns that revenue may not grow in line with infrastructure investment for AI/cloud. No specific capex figure appears in this section (quantification likely in financial statements/MD&A).

3. SUPPLIER CONCENTRATION (Severity 3): GPU/server component dependency explicitly called out for AI datacenter expansion, with acknowledgment that competitors use the same suppliers (pointing to NVIDIA as the likely single-source risk, though NVIDIA is not named in this section).

4. IRS TAX DISPUTE (Severity 3): $28.9B NOPAs from IRS for 2004-2013 tax years on intercompany transfer pricing — a specific, quantified contingent liability.

5. NATION-STATE CYBERATTACK: Previously disclosed incident (Nov 2023) involving source code repository access — ongoing risk cited with forward-looking concern about continued adversary use of stolen information.

6. AI EXPORT CONTROLS: Rescinded AI Diffusion Rule and potential replacement rulemakings flagged as material business risk.

7. GOODWILL IMPAIRMENT RISK: Activision Blizzard acquisition (Oct 2023) cited in context of integration and goodwill impairment risk.

No new SPV/off-balance-sheet entities, no new named investment counterparties beyond OpenAI and Activision Blizzard, were identified in this section.
[chunk 2/2] Section reviewed: MSFT 10-Q Part II Item 1A (Risk Factors, interim) and Item 2 (Share Repurchases), filing date 2026-01-28. No SIFI-material entities found. The text contains only generic/boilerplate risk disclosures (geopolitical risk, catastrophic events, climate change, FX hedging, labor/unionization) with no named counterparties, no specific investment disclosures, no SPV/off-balance-sheet arrangements, no customer/supplier concentration data, no AI lab relationships, and no capex commitments.
